benchmark.category: a mobile-first voice-ordering fireworks Shot Kit app with a moderated crew video wall
benchmark.users: TikTok dancers and small film crews in Phnom Penh building 15-second firework shots and posting their shoot clips

requirements.statement: admin+clerk_test@boomdrop.dev and member+clerk_test@boomdrop.dev both sign in with the password Boomdrop-test-123! and both hold role member, while swarnimsandeep@yahoo.com is the only stored user with role admin.
requirements.notes: Required credentials state the admin test account is intentionally NO LONGER admin and only swarnimsandeep@yahoo.com is; later phases must not expect admin+clerk_test to approve clips and may seed approved clips directly in Mongo.

requirements.statement: The only account allowed to approve or reject clips is swarnimsandeep@yahoo.com; GET /api/admin/clips and POST /api/admin/clips/{id}/approve or /reject return 403 to every other signed-in account, including admin+clerk_test@boomdrop.dev and any other yahoo.com or gmail.com address, return no pending clip, and no account becomes admin by being the first to sign in.
requirements.notes: Supersedes the earlier answer 'yahoo or gmail'; the later exact address is the only allowlist entry, and the agent report says first-user-becomes-admin has been removed. A signed-in outsider must receive no pending clip data with the 403.

requirements.statement: PATCH /api/admin/users/{id}/role changes a user's role only when the caller is swarnimsandeep@yahoo.com; every other signed-in account, including admin+clerk_test@boomdrop.dev, receives 403 and changes no role even when the body asks for role=admin, demoting the only remaining admin returns 409 and changes nothing, and a role field in a sign-up or profile body is ignored except through this endpoint.
requirements.notes: Build test list names PATCH role=admin being 403 for the demoted test account and demoting the only admin returning 409; the exact-email caller rule comes from the same window.

requirements.statement: GET /api/clips returns only approved, non-deleted clips, each with id, crew_name, kit_id (empty when none), posted time and week_likes, sorted by week_likes descending then newest first; it also returns top_crews with each crew's week like total highest first and clip_of_week holding the approved non-deleted clip with the highest week_likes posted in the last 7 days (ties by newest first, null when no approved clip exists); an empty store returns empty arrays and clip_of_week null.
requirements.notes: Extends the inherited wall payload for the user's Clip of the Week banner and Open this Shot Kit link; kit_id lets a clip resolve to its kit via GET /api/shot-kit/{id}, and the banner's clip must equal the top-ranked approved clip.

requirements.source_phrase: Lock clip review to my own email so nobody else can become admin on the live app
requirements.statement: Signing in as admin+clerk_test@boomdrop.dev and opening /admin shows an explicit no-access message, renders no pending clips or approve/reject controls, and /api/me for that session reports role member, so only swarnimsandeep@yahoo.com can review clips.
requirements.notes: Build test list says admin+clerk_test now gets role member from /api/me and 403 from the admin routes; the screen must not mount the review queue for a demoted account.

requirements.source_phrase: Lock clip review to my own email so nobody else can become admin on the live app
requirements.statement: An account that is not swarnimsandeep@yahoo.com is never assigned the admin role, even when it is the first account to sign in on a fresh deployment, and GET /api/me for it returns role member rather than admin.
requirements.notes: The earlier answer 'skip this for now' would have made the first sign-in admin; the later exact-email instruction reverses it, and the agent report says first-user-becomes-admin has been removed.

requirements.statement: The backend reads the reviewer allowlist from ADMIN_EMAIL in backend/.env, which is set to swarnimsandeep@yahoo.com, and grants admin only to that exact address, so a yahoo.com or gmail.com domain or a changed display name grants no admin.
requirements.notes: Required credentials say ADMIN_EMAIL must not be changed and only swarnimsandeep@yahoo.com is admin; this is the seed/config requirement later phases use instead of expecting the test accounts to approve.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a progress bar and a clear warning when a shoot video is longer than one minute
requirements.statement: Choosing a shoot video longer than 60 seconds in the upload panel shows a visible warning (data-testid long-video-warning) naming the 60-second limit and offering three actions — keep the first minute, keep the full video, and cancel to choose a shorter clip — and no upload starts until the user chooses.
requirements.notes: Build test list names long-video-warning with three buttons and cancel resetting; the warning must precede the upload rather than appear after a silent cut.

requirements.source_phrase: Warn, then keep the first minute; Keep the full video; Block it and ask for a shorter clip
requirements.statement: Choosing 'Post the first minute' for a longer-than-60-second video uploads only the first 60 seconds; choosing 'Keep the full video' uploads the full length; choosing the cancel/short-clip action leaves no file selected and uploads nothing, and the chosen mode stays visible while the upload runs.
requirements.notes: The answer lists all three choices, so offering only one of them is a missing feature; the build test list exercises Cancel and 'Post the first minute'.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a progress bar and a clear warning when a shoot video is longer than one minute
requirements.statement: While a shoot video uploads, the upload panel shows a progress bar with a numeric percent that advances from above 0 to 100 (data-testid upload-progress), disables the upload control for the duration, and on success shows a 'Sent for review' toast.
requirements.notes: Build test list names upload-progress and the toast; the percent must come from upload progress events, not a fake timer.

requirements.statement: Choosing a shoot video of 60 seconds or less shows no long-video warning, starts the upload with the progress bar and ends with the 'Sent for review' toast, so the warning is not shown to every upload.
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of the >1-minute warning: build test list explicitly checks a short video gets no warning and a progress bar.

requirements.source_phrase: Warn, then keep the first minute; Keep the full video; Block it and ask for a shorter clip
requirements.statement: POST /api/clips for a video longer than 60 seconds stores exactly the length the request selects: keep=first_minute stores a playable clip of about 60 seconds, keep=full stores the full source length, and a longer-than-60-second upload with neither choice is refused with a 4xx and stores no clip rather than being silently truncated.
requirements.notes: Build test list probes POST /api/clips with keep=first_minute and keep=full; measure the stored file duration rather than the response status, and confirm no row/blob is left on the refused path.

requirements.source_phrase: Feature the week's most-liked clip in a big banner at the top of the wall
requirements.statement: At the top of the Crew Video Wall a clip-of-week banner (data-testid clip-of-week-banner) shows the approved clip with the highest week_likes, its crew name, its current like count, a like control and a clip-of-week-open-kit link when that clip has a kit_id; liking from the banner increments the displayed count once and fills the control, and the banner is hidden when no approved clip exists.
requirements.notes: Build features list names clip-of-week-banner, clip-of-week-open-kit and liking from the banner; the banner's clip must be the top-liked approved clip of the last 7 days, not merely the newest.

requirements.source_phrase: Let viewers tap a wall clip to open the exact Shot Kit that crew used
requirements.statement: Every wall grid clip carrying a kit_id shows an 'Open this Shot Kit' link (data-testid crew-clip-open-kit-N); activating it navigates to /?kit=<kit_id> and loads that exact kit's Shot Kit card, while a clip with no kit_id shows no such link.
requirements.notes: Build features list names crew-clip-open-kit-N and the /?kit=id navigation; the loaded card must be the clip's kit, not the most recently built one, so the link carries the stored kit_id.

requirements.source_phrase: Let uploaders pick one of their kits; Only clips posted from a kit preview
requirements.statement: The real-shoot upload panel offers a kit selector (data-testid upload-shoot-kit-select) listing the kits built on this device, marks the chosen kit, and sends its kit_id with the upload; a clip posted from a preview recording carries its kit_id automatically even when no kit is picked, and a clip stored with no kit_id shows no Open this Shot Kit link.
requirements.notes: The answer chose both options; build test list says upload-shoot-kit-select shows the built kit and db.clips stores kit_id, and real uploads without a kit must still post.

requirements.statement: At 390x844 the real-shoot upload panel, its long-video warning and the clip-of-week banner render without page-level horizontal overflow, clipped buttons or overlap with each other or the wall grid, and the three warning actions plus the banner's like and open-kit controls stay tappable.
requirements.notes: Build test list names the 390px layout of the upload panel, warning and banner; this is the layout class for the newly added wall surfaces.
